items.readable_text:
Content:
The distributive law states that multiplying a group of terms by a number is the same as multiplying each term separately by that same number and adding the products.

Content:
For example, let's take a look at the following expression:

Content:
[MATH: 2(3+4).]

Content:
We can evaluate this expression using the distributive law:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/23586c10e3598384c3c2a1d23d916d90]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 2(3 + 4)|=; 2 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ 4|=; 6 + 8|=; 14|.]

Content:
The distributive law also applies when the multiplication occurs on the right of the parentheses:

Content:
[MATH: (3 + 4) ⋅ 2|=; 3 ⋅ 2 + 4 ⋅ 2|=; 6 + 8|=; 14]

Content:
The distributive law also works when there is subtraction inside the parentheses.

Content:
For example, we can expand the expression [MATH: 2(3-4)] as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/31bdd08501d1684bcf9c165278cd126c]

Content:
Notice that we keep a plus ([MATH: +]) sign between the two terms. This helps us to avoid mistakes when multiplying with negative numbers.

Content:
Now, evaluating our expression, we have

Content:
[MATH: 2(3 − 4)|=; 2 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ (− 4)|=; (6) + (− 8)|=; 6 − 8|=; − 2|.]

Content:
Finally, the distributive law also applies when the multiplication occurs on the right of the parentheses:

Content:
[MATH: (3 − 4) ⋅ 2|=; 3 ⋅ 2 + (− 4) ⋅ 2|=; (6) + (− 8)|=; 6 − 8|=; − 2|.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The distributive law states that multiplying a group of terms by a number is the same as multiplying each term separately by that same number and adding the products.

Content:
For example, let's take a look at the following expression:

Content:
[MATH: 2(3+4).]

Content:
We can evaluate this expression using the distributive law:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/23586c10e3598384c3c2a1d23d916d90]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 2(3 + 4)|=; 2 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ 4|=; 6 + 8|=; 14|.]

Content:
The distributive law also applies when the multiplication occurs on the right of the parentheses:

Content:
[MATH: (3 + 4) ⋅ 2|=; 3 ⋅ 2 + 4 ⋅ 2|=; 6 + 8|=; 14]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Dealing With a Minus Inside the Parentheses

Content:
The distributive law also works when there is subtraction inside the parentheses.

Content:
For example, we can expand the expression [MATH: 2(3-4)] as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/31bdd08501d1684bcf9c165278cd126c]

Content:
Notice that we keep a plus ([MATH: +]) sign between the two terms. This helps us to avoid mistakes when multiplying with negative numbers.

Content:
Now, evaluating our expression, we have

Content:
[MATH: 2(3 − 4)|=; 2 ⋅ 3 + 2 ⋅ (− 4)|=; (6) + (− 8)|=; 6 − 8|=; − 2|.]

Content:
Finally, the distributive law also applies when the multiplication occurs on the right of the parentheses:

Content:
[MATH: (3 − 4) ⋅ 2|=; 3 ⋅ 2 + (− 4) ⋅ 2|=; (6) + (− 8)|=; 6 − 8|=; − 2|.]
